problem_statements.title: Device-Free WiFi Sensing & Movement Analytics
problem_statements.domain: Ambient Intelligence, Smart Buildings, & Privacy-Preserving Sensing
problem_statements.description:
Primary Goal: Detect human presence, count occupants, and classify activities/falls using off-the-shelf WiFi Channel State Information (CSI) without relying on cameras, microphones, or wearables.

1. Business Context & Problem Description

Traditional occupancy and activity monitoring rely heavily on optical cameras or wearable sensors, raising severe privacy concerns, high hardware costs, and maintenance hurdles. WiFi Channel State Information (CSI) measures the amplitude and phase disturbances caused by human movement in RF multipath propagation fields. Leveraging standard WiFi signals enables non-line-of-sight (NLOS) sensing through walls while maintaining complete privacy.

2. Core Objectives

Ingest and parse raw CSI/RSSI telemetry from standard WiFi hardware (e.g., ESP32 with CSI firmware or Raspberry Pi with Nexmon patch).

Perform signal conditioning to eliminate environmental drift, high-frequency noise, and phase distortion.

Train lightweight edge machine learning models to classify ambient state variations (e.g., empty room, static person, walking, falling, occupant count).

Deploy real-time inference on low-power edge nodes (TinyML) without cloud dependencies.

3. Key Technical Challenges

Low Signal-to-Noise Ratio (SNR): Multipath fading, environmental static noise, and wall attenuation obscure subtle human motion signals.

Hardware & Phase Instability: Carrier frequency offset (CFO) and sampling time offset (STO) in consumer WiFi chipsets cause non-stationary phase noise.

Edge Resource Constraints: Executing signal preprocessing and Deep Learning inference within the tight memory and CPU constraints of ESP32/Raspberry Pi microcontrollers.

4. Technical Requirements & Deliverables

CSI Data Ingestion & Preprocessing Pipeline: Real-time signal filtering framework incorporating Hampel filters, Principal Component Analysis (PCA), and wavelet denoising.

Edge Deep Learning Model: Lightweight classification architecture (e.g., 1D CNN-LSTM or MobileNet-1D) trained on calibrated CSI feature maps.

TinyML Runtime Deployment: Quantized model artifact (TFLite Micro/ONNX) running locally on ESP32/Raspberry Pi edge hardware.

5. Evaluation Metrics & Success Criteria

problem_statements.title: Secure Examination Paper Storage & Transit System
problem_statements.domain: Education Governance, IoT Security, & Supply Chain Safeguarding
problem_statements.description:
Primary Goal: Prevent question paper leaks during storage and transit using smart sensor-equipped containers, dynamic electronic locking, real-time telemetry, and immutable audit logs.

1. Business Context & Problem Description

High-stakes academic and recruitment examinations frequently face compromises due to physical tampering during storage and transit. Manual lock-and-key protocols and offline surveillance fail to provide proactive breach visibility. An IoT-based secure ecosystem provides real-time tracking, environmental verification, tamper detection, and immediate security escalation.

2. Core Objectives

Design tamper-proof smart storage containers equipped with electronic locks, GPS tracking, and environmental sensors.

Enforce multi-factor authentication (MFA) and geofenced access policies for authorized personnel.

Stream continuous container health (location, lid status, vibration/tilt, ambient conditions) to a central cloud dashboard.

Maintain an immutable audit log of every access event to ensure complete chain-of-custody accountability.

3. Key Technical Challenges

Intermittent Connectivity: Maintaining telemetry logging and security integrity during transportation across rural or low-network zones.

Physical Tamper Evasion: Detecting sophisticated intrusion attempts (e.g., side-casing breach, lock bypass, sensor spoofing).

Power Management: Ensuring continuous operation across multi-day transit routes using low-power IoT architectures.

4. Technical Requirements & Deliverables

Smart Enclosure Telematics Module: Hardware node integrating cellular/GPS, micro-switches, optical light sensors, accelerometers, and solenoid locks.

Immutable Audit Engine: Cryptographically verified event ledger logging access requests, location stamps, and sensor triggers.

Central Command Dashboard: Web/mobile monitoring platform with automated real-time alert dispatching (SMS, Email, Push) upon breach detection.

5. Evaluation Metrics & Success Criteria

problem_statements.title: IoT Smart Reverse Vending Machine (Bottle Crusher)
problem_statements.domain: Smart Cities, Environmental Sustainability, & Circular Economy
problem_statements.description:
Primary Goal: Automate plastic bottle detection, reject non-recyclable contaminants, reduce waste volume via mechanical crushing, and motivate citizens through integrated reward programs.

1. Business Context & Problem Description

Public recycling bins suffer from high contamination rates due to non-plastic waste (metal cans, glass, organic trash) mixed with recyclable PET bottles. Furthermore, uncompressed bottles rapidly fill bin capacity, leading to frequent logistics overruns. An automated Reverse Vending Machine (RVM) validates materials, compacts waste, and incentivizes recycling through instant user rewards.

2. Core Objectives

Distinguish PET plastic bottles from non-plastic materials (metals, glass, cardboard) at the point of insertion.

Mechanically crush accepted plastic containers to reduce storage volume by up to .

Attribute recycling contributions to individual user accounts and disburse rewards (points, cashback, coupons).

Stream real-time operational status (bin fill level, crusher motor health, user activity) to a cloud management dashboard.

3. Key Technical Challenges

Rapid Material Sorting: Accurate multi-sensor verification (inductive, capacitive, optical, or vision-based) within milliseconds.

Mechanical Reliability: Preventing motor jams, blade binding, and safely handling fluids remaining in bottles.

Anti-Fraud Mechanisms: Preventing string-tethered bottle re-insertion and duplicate reward claims.

4. Technical Requirements & Deliverables

Material Verification Assembly: Multi-sensor array and lightweight vision classifier detecting plastic vs. metal/glass.

Crusher Control System: Industrial actuator/motor controller equipped with auto-reverse anti-jamming logic.

User Rewards Platform: Interactive touch frontend with mobile backend integration for instant wallet/reward credit.

IoT Fleet Management Dashboard: Cloud portal monitoring fill levels, maintenance alerts, and aggregate recycling analytics.

5. Evaluation Metrics & Success Criteria

problem_statements.title: AI Road Construction Material & Granulometry Inspection
problem_statements.domain: Civil Engineering, Construction Quality Assurance, & Computer Vision
problem_statements.description:
Primary Goal: Automatically identify road construction raw materials and estimate aggregate stone chip size distributions in real time using computer vision and deep learning.

1. Business Context & Problem Description

The structural lifespan and load distribution of asphalt roads depend heavily on aggregate gradation (stone chip size mix). Manual sieve analysis and visual site inspections are labor-intensive, slow, and subjective. Deploying a camera-based AI inspection system provides continuous, non-destructive quality control directly on site.

2. Core Objectives

Classify road construction raw materials (e.g., stone aggregates, sand, gravel, bitumen mixes) from camera imagery.

Segment individual stone chips and estimate their size categories (e.g., , , ) using computer vision.

Compare measured aggregate distributions against standardized engineering sieve specs.

Transmit automated quality logs to a centralized engineering cloud portal.

3. Key Technical Challenges

Particle Overlap & Occlusion: Disambiguating dense, overlapping aggregate piles on conveyor belts or dump beds.

Environmental Variance: Handling unstable outdoor lighting, shadows, surface moisture, and dust buildup on camera lenses.

Scale Calibration: Maintaining millimeter-level spatial resolution without manual physical reference markers.

4. Technical Requirements & Deliverables

Optical Image Acquisition Rig: Enclosed camera and LED illumination setup for consistent field captures.

Computer Vision Granulometry Pipeline: Instance segmentation model (e.g., Mask R-CNN, YOLO-Seg) combined with ellipse fitting for particle axis sizing.

QA Analytics Dashboard: Desktop/cloud application generating material classification reports and cumulative pass-through sieve curves.

5. Evaluation Metrics & Success Criteria

problem_statements.title: Autonomous Public Toilet Maintenance & Hygiene System
problem_statements.domain: Smart Cities, Facility Management, & IoT Automation
problem_statements.description:
Primary Goal: Continuous hygiene monitoring, automated self-cleaning and disinfection cycles, odor mitigation, and demand-driven janitorial dispatch for public toilets.

1. Business Context & Problem Description

Public sanitation facilities often deteriorate due to static, scheduled cleaning regimes that ignore actual footfall and usage intensity. Unmanaged odors, empty soap/water reservoirs, and unhygienic surfaces lead to poor public health outcomes. An autonomous IoT ecosystem cleans dynamically post-usage and dispatches janitorial staff based on real-time sensory thresholds.

2. Core Objectives

Monitor facility usage count, air quality (), water levels, and consumable capacity via dynamic IoT sensors.

Automate touchless post-use flushing, floor washing, and aerosol disinfection based on occupancy triggers.

Actuate automated ventilation fans and deodorizer dispensers when gas levels cross safety thresholds.

Stream telemetry to a cloud dashboard to optimize janitorial shifts according to dynamic demand.

3. Key Technical Challenges

Harsh Operating Environment: Sensor degradation caused by high humidity, corrosive cleaning chemicals, and splashing.

False Occupancy Triggers: Preventing automated cleaning routines while a user is still present inside the cubicle.

Resource Optimization: Balancing aggressive sanitation cycles against water and electricity conservation constraints.

4. Technical Requirements & Deliverables

Multi-Sensor IoT Array: Water-proof sensor cluster (ToF/PIR occupancy, /VOC gas sensors, ultrasonic level indicators).

Automated Actuator Unit: Relays controlling solenoid water valves, floor wash spray nozzles, and ventilation fans.

Smart Facility Dashboard: Web platform and mobile app delivering real-time status alerts and dynamic staff routing schedules.

5. Evaluation Metrics & Success Criteria

problem_statements.title: IoT Electromagnetic Radiation (EMR) Monitoring System
problem_statements.domain: Occupational Health & Safety, Environmental Sensing, & Industrial IoT
problem_statements.description:
Primary Goal: Continuously measure indoor electromagnetic radiation (EMR), generate real-time spatial heatmaps, compare exposure against regulatory safety limits, and issue exposure mitigation alerts.

1. Business Context & Problem Description

The proliferation of Wi-Fi access points, cellular towers, high-voltage infrastructure, and industrial electronics elevates electromagnetic field (EMF) exposure in workplaces and residences. Periodic manual inspections fail to catch transient spikes. Continuous IoT monitoring provides clear visibility into EMR hotspots and supports compliance with health standards (e.g., ICNIRP/IEEE).

2. Core Objectives

Measure high-frequency RF and low-frequency ELF field intensity continuously across indoor facilities.

Aggregate field measurements via IoT gateway nodes and stream spatial data to a central platform.

Render real-time 2D/3D indoor radiation heatmaps highlighting hotspot zones.

Issue immediate alerts and actionable safety recommendations when limits are breached.

3. Key Technical Challenges

Wideband Sensor Calibration: Maintaining high measurement linearity across a broad frequency spectrum ( to ).

Spatial Interpolation: Generating accurate indoor EMR continuous heatmaps from a finite set of discrete sensor nodes.

Signal Interference: Filtering out localized electrostatic or temporary non-hazardous transients without missing true safety violations.

4. Technical Requirements & Deliverables

Multi-Band EMR Sensor Probe: IoT sensing hardware measuring E-field (), H-field (), and power density ().

Heatmap Analytics Engine: Cloud processing pipeline using Kriging or Radial Basis Function (RBF) spatial interpolation algorithms.

Compliance & Alert Portal: Web application displaying live room layouts, safety threshold overlays, and exposure duration tracking.

5. Evaluation Metrics & Success Criteria

problem_statements.title: AI-Powered Railway Level Crossing Safety System
problem_statements.domain: Intelligent Transportation Systems, Railway Safety, & Computer Vision
problem_statements.description:
Primary Goal: Detect vehicles, pedestrians, and animals trapped in railway crossing danger zones in real time using edge AI, issuing instant collision-prevention warnings to control rooms.

1. Business Context & Problem Description

Unmanned and congested railway level crossings are high-risk zones for severe accidents caused by stranded vehicles or trespassing pedestrians. Traditional physical barriers cannot detect obstacles trapped inside the gate perimeter after closure. Vision-based edge monitoring automatically flags hazards in real time, preventing derailments and saving lives.

2. Core Objectives

Continuously monitor the level crossing grid area using optical/thermal vision sensors.

Detect and classify trapped obstacles (vehicles, humans, livestock, heavy debris) inside the danger zone.

Generate instant high-priority alerts to station control rooms and incoming train telemetry systems upon hazard detection.

Log video evidence and event metrics to a central railway analytics portal.

3. Key Technical Challenges

All-Weather Reliability: Sustaining high target detection accuracy in dense fog, heavy rain, night darkness, and direct sun glare.

Ultra-Low False Alarm Rate: Preventing false emergency train halts while maintaining zero missed detection tolerance.

Edge Processing Speed: Executing object detection and tracking algorithms locally with sub-second transmission delays.

4. Technical Requirements & Deliverables

Ruggedized Edge Processing Unit: Outdoor edge AI hardware (e.g., NVIDIA Jetson / Industrial IPC) running object detection models.

Deep Learning Vision Engine: Object detection and multi-object tracking pipeline (e.g., YOLOv8 + ByteTRACK) calibrated to the crossing zone.

IoT Wireless Alert Gateway: Fail-safe, low-latency communications module (LTE/LoRa/GSM) broadcasting to railway control systems.

5. Evaluation Metrics & Success Criteria

problem_statements.title: IoT Smart Bridge Structural Health Monitoring (SHM)
problem_statements.domain: Infrastructure Civil Engineering, Predictive Maintenance, & Industrial IoT
problem_statements.description:
Primary Goal: Continuously evaluate bridge structural integrity using multi-sensor IoT networks to detect tilt, strain, crack expansion, and abnormal vibrations before critical failures occur.

1. Business Context & Problem Description

Bridges suffer from material fatigue, heavy traffic overloads, corrosion, and seismic activity. Periodic visual inspections are infrequent, labor-intensive, and unable to detect internal structural decay. Continuous IoT Structural Health Monitoring (SHM) enables real-time dynamic assessment, early flaw detection, and cost-effective predictive maintenance schedules.

2. Core Objectives

Deploy synchronized wireless sensors across structural spans to measure strain, vibration, tilt, displacement, and environmental parameters.

Aggregate high-frequency dynamic telemetry via edge gateways for real-time modal analysis.

Detect structural anomalies by comparing active vibration frequencies and strain profiles against baseline physics models.

Provide early alerts and long-term lifespan degradation trends on a central engineering platform.

3. Key Technical Challenges

High-Frequency Data Synchronization: Precision time-stamping (sub-millisecond synchronization) across distributed sensor nodes across long bridge spans.

Noise Separation: Distinguishing ambient traffic vibration from true structural stiffness degradation or cracking.

Sensor Node Longevity: Ensuring uninterrupted node operation in remote outdoor locations using low-power design and energy harvesting.

4. Technical Requirements & Deliverables

Structural Sensor Node Mesh: Wireless nodes incorporating tri-axial accelerometers, strain gauges, inclinometers, and temperature sensors.

Edge Fast Fourier Transform (FFT) Module: Edge computing engine extracting modal frequencies, damping ratios, and peak accelerations.

Cloud Predictive SHM Dashboard: Engineering platform featuring dynamic baseline comparison, anomaly notifications, and structural health scoring.

5. Evaluation Metrics & Success Criteria

problem_statements.title: Autonomous Floating Waste Collection & Water Monitoring Robot
problem_statements.domain: Autonomous Marine Systems, Environmental Robotics, & Water Quality Sensing
problem_statements.description:
Primary Goal: Automate surface plastic/debris harvesting in urban water bodies while simultaneously measuring water quality parameters and mapping spatial pollution hotspots.

1. Business Context & Problem Description

Floating plastic waste and organic debris choke urban lakes, rivers, and canals, leading to ecosystem degradation, blocked drainage, and severe public health risks. Manual cleaning boats are costly and impractical for continuous maintenance. An autonomous robotic vessel cleans surface debris continuously while generating comprehensive spatial water quality reports.

2. Core Objectives

Autonomously navigate surface water bodies while avoiding static and dynamic obstacles.

Capture and collect floating plastic, foam, and organic trash into an onboard containment basket.

Sense key water quality indicators (pH, turbidity, temperature, Dissolved Oxygen, Total Dissolved Solids) in real time.

Map GPS-tagged pollution heatmaps and stream operational analytics to a cloud monitoring portal.

3. Key Technical Challenges

Unpredictable Aquatic Navigation: Navigating around floating debris fields, dense water weeds, shallow depths, and varying water currents.

Sensory Bio-Fouling: Preventing algae and residue buildup from degrading probe accuracy during extended deployments.

Power Management: Balancing motor propulsion and conveyor belt harvesting consumption against battery constraints.

4. Technical Requirements & Deliverables

Autonomous Unmanned Surface Vessel (USV): Catamaran or twin-hull platform fitted with a conveyor/skimmer mechanism and GPS navigation.

Environmental Sensor Payload: Water-quality probe unit measuring pH, turbidity, DO, TDS, and water temperature.

Cloud Telemetry & Mapping Portal: Geospatial dashboard rendering vessel tracks, waste collection metrics, and water quality spatial maps.

5. Evaluation Metrics & Success Criteria

problem_statements.title: Interactive AI Robotic Companion for Children
problem_statements.domain: Consumer AI, Educational Robotics, & Human-Robot Interaction (HRI)
problem_statements.description:
Primary Goal: Reduce passive screen time in children by driving engagement through an interactive, voice-first robotic companion providing physical games, storytelling, and personalized learning.

1. Business Context & Problem Description

Excessive screen time negatively impacts children's eyesight, physical health, sleep patterns, and social development. Parents struggle to find screen-free alternatives that hold a child's interest. An intelligent, voice-interactive robotic companion actively encourages physical movement, creative problem solving, and screen-free play habits.

2. Core Objectives

Enable natural, age-appropriate conversational interactions using voice recognition, NLP, and speech synthesis.

Deliver interactive learning experiences, including movement-based games, storytelling, dance, quizzes, and music.

Personalize activity difficulty and content based on the child's age, interests, and developmental milestones.

Track daily screen-free engagement and deliver actionable developmental insights to parents via a mobile app.

3. Key Technical Challenges

Child Speech Recognition (Acoustics): Handling unique pitch, varying accents, incomplete grammar, and background noise typical of child speech.

Low Response Latency: Maintaining natural, conversational cadence without long pauses during LLM/voice generation calls.

Privacy & Safety Safeguards: Strict adherence to child data privacy standards (e.g., COPPA/GDPR-K) with on-device hardware privacy switches.

4. Technical Requirements & Deliverables

Robotic Hardware Platform: Compact robotic shell with expressive display/LEDs, omnidirectional microphone array, speaker, and mobility actuators.

Child-Centric Conversational Agent: Conversational AI pipeline with content filtering, speech synthesis, and adaptive gameplay logic.

Parental Companion Mobile App: Mobile interface for setting screen-free goals, reviewing activity summaries, and managing content filters.

5. Evaluation Metrics & Success Criteria

problem_statements.title: IoT Smart Cold Chain Temperature & Spoilage Monitor
problem_statements.description:
Primary Goal: Track ambient conditions in cold storage units during transport using low-cost sensor nodes to predict food spoilage and trigger immediate temperature alerts.

1. Business Context & Problem Description

Perishable items like dairy, pharmaceuticals, and fresh produce require continuous temperature and humidity control during transport. Breakdowns in refrigeration systems or unmonitored transit delays lead to massive financial losses and public health risks. Continuous, low-cost environmental logging prevents inventory loss before goods arrive damaged.

2. Core Objectives

Continuously log temperature, humidity, and volatile organic compound (VOC) levels inside transport containers.

Compute dynamic shelf-life decay using Arrhenius kinetic models on edge microcontrollers.

Transmit real-time geolocation and environmental breach alerts over cellular or LoRa networks.

Maintain an automated chain-of-custody compliance report for quality control audits.

3. Key Technical Challenges

Power Optimization: Operating nodes on battery power for extended multi-day trips.

Network Blackouts: Buffering telemetry data locally during cellular dead zones without data loss.

Sensor Drift Calibration: Maintaining temperature accuracy within  using basic sensors like the DHT22 or DS18B20.

4. Technical Requirements & Deliverables

Hardware: ESP32 / Arduino Nano, DS18B20/DHT22 temperature sensors, MQ-135 air quality sensor, SIM800L GSM/GPS module.

Firmware: Low-power sleep routines with local EEPROM/SD-card data buffering.

Cloud Dashboard: Web portal rendering route maps, temperature graphs, and SMS alert configuration.

5. Evaluation Metrics & Success Criteria

problem_statements.title: Computer Vision Smart Parking Space Occupancy Engine
problem_statements.description:
Primary Goal: Detect available parking spots in open-air lots using a standard USB/IP webcam and edge vision models, eliminating the need for expensive per-spot ground sensors.

1. Business Context & Problem Description

Traditional smart parking systems rely on individual magnetic ground sensors installed under every single parking bay, incurring extreme hardware and installation costs. An overhead camera paired with computer vision can monitor dozens of parking bays simultaneously, offering an affordable, scalable alternative for municipal and commercial parking management.

2. Core Objectives

Capture continuous video feeds of parking lots using standard CCTV or IP cameras.

Map bounding boxes for individual parking slots onto the camera feed via a lightweight UI setup tool.

Classify each slot as "Occupied" or "Vacant" using lightweight deep learning models.

Stream real-time availability counts to a public web portal or digital signage driver.

3. Key Technical Challenges

Occlusion & Perspective Glare: Vehicle shadows, rain reflections, and adjacent vehicle overhangs masking adjacent spots.

Day-to-Night Transitions: Maintaining high classification accuracy under extreme lighting changes.

Edge Processing Limits: Running inference across  parking slots per camera frame on a Raspberry Pi.

4. Technical Requirements & Deliverables

Hardware: Raspberry Pi 4 / PC workstation, generic USB/RTSP IP Camera.

Vision Pipeline: OpenCV region-of-interest (ROI) mapper paired with a lightweight image classifier (e.g., MobileNetV2 or custom CNN).

Signage API Engine: Lightweight REST API streaming current slot capacity to mobile apps and LED displays.

5. Evaluation Metrics & Success Criteria

problem_statements.title: Edge AI Acoustic Transformer Fault Inspector
problem_statements.description:
Primary Goal: Detect early mechanical and electrical faults in motors, transformers, and pumps by analyzing operational acoustic signatures using a low-cost microphone and edge AI.

1. Business Context & Problem Description

Industrial equipment like transformers, induction motors, and compressors generate subtle changes in sound and hum frequencies prior to mechanical failure. Routine manual listener checks miss high-frequency bearing chatter or electrical arcing. Continuous acoustic monitoring using low-cost edge nodes flags abnormal operating frequencies before catastrophic breakdowns occur.

2. Core Objectives

Capture acoustic emissions from heavy machinery using a standard MEMS microphone.

Convert raw audio signals into Mel-spectrogram frequency representations in real time.

Train an anomaly detection model (e.g., Autoencoder or MobileNet-Audio) to recognize normal operational hum vs. early wear patterns.

Trigger maintenance warnings on local indicator LEDs and remote dashboards when sound signatures deviate from baseline.

3. Key Technical Challenges

Background Factory Noise: Filtering out ambient plant noises, background voices, and nearby vehicle sounds.

Acoustic Drift: Distinguishing benign load changes from structural component wear.

On-Device Feature Extraction: Executing real-time Fast Fourier Transforms (FFT) and spectrogram generation on constrained microcontrollers.

4. Technical Requirements & Deliverables

Hardware: ESP32 / Raspberry Pi Pico, INMP441 I2S MEMS Microphone module.

Edge Audio Pipeline: On-device FFT and Mel-spectrogram generator running in C++/TinyML.

Anomaly Engine: Unsupervised reconstruction loss model identifying acoustic deviations beyond baseline variance.

5. Evaluation Metrics & Success Criteria

problem_statements.title: Smart Agriculture Soil Moisture & Dynamic Irrigation System
problem_statements.description:
Primary Goal: Optimize agricultural water usage by automatically scheduling drip irrigation based on real-time soil moisture sensors, weather forecasts, and crop types.

1. Business Context & Problem Description

Over-watering damages crop yields, wastes groundwater reserves, and swells electricity costs for farmers. Conventional automated systems rely on basic timers that irrigate regardless of actual soil moisture or impending rainfall. A dynamic IoT system balances soil readings with local weather predictions to deliver precise water volumes.

2. Core Objectives

Measure volumetric water content and temperature at root level using corrosion-resistant soil sensors.

Fetch local open-source weather predictions to delay scheduled watering if rain is imminent.

Actuate solenoid water valves via relay modules to irrigate specific farm zones autonomously.

Monitor pump power usage and alert farmers to dry-run or pipe leak anomalies.

3. Key Technical Challenges

Sensor Corrosion: Preventing fast oxidation in cheap capacitive/resistive soil probes.

Power-Efficient Field Deployment: Operating outdoor field nodes using small solar panels and rechargeable batteries.

Soil Heterogeneity: Calibrating sensor moisture thresholds across clay, sand, and loam soils.

4. Technical Requirements & Deliverables

Hardware: ESP8266 / ESP32, Capacitive Soil Moisture Sensor v1.2, 5V Relay Module, 12V Solenoid Valve, 5W Solar Panel with TP4056 charger.

Control Pipeline: Multi-variable decision engine integrating sensor moisture bounds and weather API triggers.

Mobile Interface: WhatsApp/Telegram bot or simple web app for manual valve overrides and daily water logs.

5. Evaluation Metrics & Success Criteria

problem_statements.title: AI Computer Vision Worker PPE Compliance Monitor
problem_statements.description:
Primary Goal: Verify that workers on construction sites and manufacturing floors are wearing mandatory Personal Protective Equipment (PPE) like hardhats and safety vests using CCTV feeds.

1. Business Context & Problem Description

Workplace accidents on industrial sites frequently stem from non-compliance with Personal Protective Equipment (PPE) mandates. Manual visual monitoring by site managers is intermittent and difficult to maintain across large sites. An automated computer vision system continuously checks compliance and generates immediate site safety scores.

2. Core Objectives

Stream video feeds from affordable RTSP security cameras across site access points.

Detect workers and classify whether mandatory items (safety helmets, high-visibility vests) are correctly worn.

Trigger local audio alarms when unhelmeted workers enter designated hazardous zones.

Generate daily compliance reports highlighting non-compliance hotspots for safety managers.

3. Key Technical Challenges

Distance & Resolution Limits: Detecting small hardhats on workers walking far from low-cost camera lenses.

Extreme Occlusion: Workers carrying equipment or bending over masking safety vest coverage.

Real-time Performance: Running object detection across multiple camera streams on low-cost hardware.

4. Technical Requirements & Deliverables

Hardware: Raspberry Pi 4 / low-cost desktop GPU workstation, generic RTSP IP Cameras / USB Webcams.

Vision Model: Fine-tuned YOLOv8-Nano / SSSD-Lite object detection model trained on hardhat/vest datasets.

Safety Dashboard: Local dashboard logging violation snapshots, timestamped records, and floor-wise risk scores.

5. Evaluation Metrics & Success Criteria

problem_statements.title: IoT Smart Energy Meter & Appliance Load Disaggregation
problem_statements.domain: Smart Grid, Home Automation, & Energy Efficiency
problem_statements.description:
Primary Goal: Monitor household current consumption in real time and estimate individual appliance usage (NIALM) using a non-invasive split-core current transformer sensor.

1. Business Context & Problem Description

High electricity bills often confuse consumers because standard energy meters show only aggregate monthly kilowatt-hours. Replacing every wall socket with a smart plug is expensive and intrusive. Non-Intrusive Load Monitoring (NILM) uses a single sensor clamped to the main electrical panel to identify individual appliance activity from total current waveforms.

2. Core Objectives

Sample current and voltage waveforms at the main circuit breaker using a non-invasive current transformer.

Calculate active power, reactive power, power factor, and cumulative energy usage on edge hardware.

Identify appliance start/stop events (e.g., refrigerator cycles, AC compressor, microwave) using electrical signature processing.

Push live power consumption metrics to a home dashboard or mobile app.

3. Key Technical Challenges

Sampling Rate Constraints: High-speed analog-to-digital sampling needed to capture transient current spikes without overloading microcontrollers.

Load Overlap: Disambiguating multiple resistive/inductive appliances operating simultaneously.

Calibration Accuracy: Ensuring current readings match utility meter standards across varying voltage conditions.

4. Technical Requirements & Deliverables

Hardware: ESP32, SCT-013-000 Non-invasive AC Current Transformer sensor, ZMPT101B Voltage Sensor module.

DSP Pipeline: Real-time RMS current/voltage computation, active/reactive power calculation, and event detection logic.

User Interface: Web dashboard displaying live power draws, daily cost metrics, and inferred appliance breakdowns.

5. Evaluation Metrics & Success Criteria

problem_statements.title: Smart LPG Gas Cylinder Leakage & Weight Monitoring System
problem_statements.domain: Home Safety, Commercial Kitchens, & Asset Management
problem_statements.description:
Primary Goal: Prevent catastrophic kitchen fires by detecting LPG gas leaks, automatically shutting off gas supply valves, and monitoring cylinder weight to predict depletion dates.

1. Business Context & Problem Description

Liquefied Petroleum Gas (LPG) leaks in home and restaurant kitchens present severe explosion and fire risks. Additionally, sudden gas depletion mid-cooking causes operational frustration. An affordable smart baseplate continuously tracks cylinder weight for timely refills while safeguarding against leaks by automatically cutting off gas flow.

2. Core Objectives

Measure combustible gas concentrations () near kitchen floor levels in real time.

Track LPG cylinder net weight using a strain-gauge load cell placed under the cylinder base.

Actuate a motorized inline gas valve to shut off supply instantly upon detecting gas leaks.

Send automated SMS/push notifications when gas level drops below  capacity.

3. Key Technical Challenges

Sensor Drift & False Alarms: MQ gas sensors respond to humidity and alcohol fumes; filtering out false triggers is critical.

Load Cell Creep: Preventing long-term mechanical drift in strain gauge readings under constant heavy weight ().

Fail-Safe Operation: Ensuring the mechanical gas shutoff operates reliably even during power outages using battery backups.

4. Technical Requirements & Deliverables

Hardware: ESP8266 / ESP32, MQ-6 Gas Sensor, HX711 Load Cell Amplifier with  Load Cell strain gauges, 12V Motorized Ball Valve, Piezo Buzzer.

Firmware: Gas concentration threshold logic, moving-average weight filtering, and automatic valve triggering routines.

Alert System: Local visual/audio alarm coupled with cloud notification services.

5. Evaluation Metrics & Success Criteria

problem_statements.title: Computer Vision Structural Concrete Crack Measurement Gauge
problem_statements.domain: Infrastructure Inspection, Civil Engineering, & Quality Control
problem_statements.description:
Primary Goal: Estimate surface crack width, orientation, and length on concrete walls and bridges using a smartphone or web camera paired with automated vision processing.

1. Business Context & Problem Description

Structural concrete inspection requires detecting hair-line surface cracks to assess building degradation. Traditional manual field measurement uses optical crack-width rulers, a process that is slow, subjective, and difficult to document digitally over time. An automated camera tool measures crack width with millimeter precision and logs spatial position.

2. Core Objectives

Capture close-up images of concrete surfaces with an affordable camera or mobile phone lens.

Segment crack boundaries from concrete texture noise using edge detection and image segmentation.

Estimate physical crack width (in millimeters) using optical scaling algorithms and reference markers.

Store inspection records with timestamped snapshots and severity tags in a digital catalog.

3. Key Technical Challenges

Surface Texture Confusion: Distinguishing narrow concrete cracks from surface dirt, stains, or formwork joints.

Sub-Millimeter Calibration: Achieving sub-millimeter measurement accuracy ( width resolution) without expensive specialized lenses.

Lighting Artifacts: Eliminating deep shadows inside cracks that distort edge detection calculations.

4. Technical Requirements & Deliverables

Hardware: Raspberry Pi 4 with Camera Module / Android Smartphone / USB Digital Microscope.

Vision Engine: OpenCV pipeline employing adaptive thresholding, Hessian matrix ridge filtering, and contour width profiling.

Reporting Module: Mobile-friendly UI displaying color-coded crack masks, calculated maximum/average widths, and exportable PDF logs.

5. Evaluation Metrics & Success Criteria

problem_statements.title: IoT Smart Water Tank Level & Leakage Controller
problem_statements.domain: Smart Buildings, Resource Conservation, & Facility Management
problem_statements.description:
Primary Goal: Prevent urban water tank overflows, measure consumption trends, detect pipe leaks, and automate pump operations using non-contact sensors.

1. Business Context & Problem Description

Water tanks in residential and commercial buildings routinely overflow due to faulty float switches or delayed manual pump shutdowns, wasting thousands of liters of clean water. Unseen pipe leaks down the line cause structural damage and high water bills. An automated IoT controller monitors levels continuously and detects pipe anomalies.

2. Core Objectives

Track overhead water tank levels in real time using non-contact ultrasonic or ToF sensors.

Actuate water pump relays based on configurable upper/lower tank capacity bounds.

Detect potential pipe leaks down the supply line by analyzing abnormal continuous flow patterns during non-peak hours.

Display water availability metrics and daily pump runtime on a local display or mobile dashboard.

3. Key Technical Challenges

Ultrasonic Echo Reflections: False distance readings caused by condensation drops on the sensor face or tank wall reflections.

Pump Surge Protection: Preventing high-frequency relay toggling when surface waves ripple inside the tank.

Wireless Range: Transmitting signals from roof-mounted tanks down through multiple concrete floor slabs to ground pumps.

4. Technical Requirements & Deliverables

Hardware: ESP32 / Arduino, JSN-SR04T Waterproof Ultrasonic Distance Sensor, YF-S201 Water Flow Sensor, 30A Heavy-Duty Relay Module.

Control Logic: Debounced moving-average level filter, dry-run pump safety shutdown, and night-time leak flow logic.

Dashboard: Web/App interface displaying current percentage full, pump status, and historical daily usage graphs.

5. Evaluation Metrics & Success Criteria

problem_statements.title: AI Edge Computer Vision Smart Solar Panel Cleaner
problem_statements.description:
Primary Goal: Detect dust and bird-dropping accumulation on solar photovoltaic (PV) panels using edge vision and trigger targeted automated wiper/brush mechanisms to restore efficiency.

1. Business Context & Problem Description

Dust, sand, and organic debris accumulation on solar panels can reduce photovoltaic power output by up to . Cleaning entire solar arrays on a fixed time schedule wastes water and accelerates mechanical wear on cleaning rigs. An AI camera system assesses actual surface soiling and triggers cleaning cycles only when necessary.

2. Core Objectives

Inspect solar panel surfaces using an automated overhead camera or mobile crawler unit.

Classify surface soiling coverage into clear, light dust, heavy dirt, or localized hotspots (e.g., bird droppings).

Trigger automated motorized wiper/water spray mechanisms across dirty panels.

Log estimated power restoration metrics post-cleaning cycle.

3. Key Technical Challenges

Direct Sun Glare: Processing high-contrast reflection images taken in direct sunlight.

Hotspot Detection: Identifying small, concentrated contaminants (like droppings) that cause localized panel overheating.

Low-Power Edge Hardware: Operating inspection and motor actuation on outdoor solar-powered edge hardware.

4. Technical Requirements & Deliverables

Hardware: ESP32-CAM / Raspberry Pi Zero 2W, 12V DC Motor Driver (L298N), Linear Actuator/Wiper motor assembly, 5V Relay.

Vision Algorithm: Lightweight image segmentation model (or OpenCV texture entropy analysis) measuring dirty vs. clean surface ratio.

Telemetry Dashboard: Remote cloud platform logging cleaning frequencies, estimated efficiency gains, and motor status.

5. Evaluation Metrics & Success Criteria

problem_statements.title: Smart Indoor Air Quality & Automated HVAC Filter Monitor
problem_statements.domain: Building Management, Environmental Health, & HVAC Automation
problem_statements.description:
Primary Goal: Monitor particulate matter (), carbon dioxide (), and humidity in indoor working spaces, dynamically controlling fresh air intake and alerting to clogged filters.

1. Business Context & Problem Description

Poor indoor air quality (IAQ) causes fatigue, lowered cognitive function, and respiratory issues among indoor workers. Running HVAC fans continuously wastes electricity, while delayed filter replacements cause system strain and poor filtration. Smart IoT nodes sense IAQ trends, regulate ventilation fans dynamically, and issue automated maintenance alerts when filters clog.

2. Core Objectives

Sample indoor particulate matter (),  levels, temperature, and relative humidity.

Sense differential pressure across HVAC air filters to detect clogging.

Control ventilation fans dynamically using PWM signals to adjust air exchange based on occupant load and gas build-up.

Push live air quality index (AQI) values to digital wall displays and building facility dashboards.

3. Key Technical Challenges

Sensor Calibration: Non-Dispersive Infrared (NDIR) sensors require baseline calibration routines to prevent drift.

Low-Noise Fan Control: Smooth PWM speed transitions without generating acoustic motor hum.

Dynamic Thresholding: Balancing energy conservation against target indoor AQI limits.

4. Technical Requirements & Deliverables

Hardware: ESP32, PMS5003 Dust Particulate Sensor, MH-Z19B NDIR  Sensor, BME280 Temp/Humidity Sensor, MOSFET PWM fan driver.

Control Loop: PID loop modulating fan speed relative to real-time  PPM and PM concentrations.

Facility UI: Real-time web portal displaying floor-wise AQI heatmaps and filter lifecycle health bars.

5. Evaluation Metrics & Success Criteria

problem_statements.title: IoT RFID & Smart Scale Inventory Automated Bin System
problem_statements.description:
Primary Goal: Track bin-level inventory of small hardware parts (screws, electronic components, fittings) using weight scale sensors and RFID tags to trigger auto-replenishment.

1. Business Context & Problem Description

Stockouts of small low-cost items (e.g., bolts, resistors, fasteners) on assembly lines halt entire manufacturing shifts. Manual stock checks are error-prone and time-consuming. Equipping storage bins with integrated strain-gauge scales and RFID readers provides real-time, automated inventory counts without manual logging.

2. Core Objectives

Measure bin weight continuously to compute precise unit counts of uniform hardware components.

Read RFID tags attached to inventory bins to automatically associate item metadata with specific shelf slots.

Trigger purchase requisitions automatically when component counts drop below predefined reorder thresholds.

Display stock counts on OLED screen modules mounted on each shelf bin.

3. Key Technical Challenges

Single-Unit Weight Resolution: Accurately detecting small weight changes when single components weigh under .

Load Cell Calibration: Auto-zeroing tare weight variations caused by changing bin containers or dust accumulation.

Bus Multiplexing: Interfacing dozens of weight scale modules to a single controller node across storage racks.

4. Technical Requirements & Deliverables

Hardware: ESP32 / Raspberry Pi, HX711 Load Cell Amplifiers with  Load Cells, RC522 RFID Reader,  I2C OLED Display.

Inventory Engine: Piece-weight calibration routine, low-stock threshold triggers, and inventory change event streaming.

Warehouse Portal: Web application managing inventory balances, SKU mappings, and purchase order triggers.

5. Evaluation Metrics & Success Criteria

problem_statements.title: Computer Vision Smart Pest & Disease Leaf Classifier
problem_statements.domain: Precision Farming, Crop Protection, & Mobile AI
problem_statements.description:
Primary Goal: Detect and classify crop leaf diseases and pest infestations in real time using a low-cost camera module and edge AI, providing immediate treatment guidance to farmers.

1. Business Context & Problem Description

Plant diseases and pest attacks cause major agricultural yield losses. Farmers often identify infection stages too late or misapply inappropriate chemical pesticides. A handheld or tractor-mounted camera tool equipped with an edge vision model identifies specific plant pathologies early and suggests precise organic or chemical remedies.

2. Core Objectives

Capture high-resolution images of crop leaves using an onboard camera or smartphone camera.

Segment diseased leaf areas and classify pathologies (e.g., powdery mildew, leaf rust, blight, pest damage).

Display localized disease names and recommended treatment steps on a simple screen interface.

Geotag infection locations on a map to track disease spread across farm fields.

3. Key Technical Challenges

Complex Outdoor Backgrounds: Isolating target leaves from background soil, weeds, and overlapping foliage.

Visual Pathology Similarities: Disambiguating early-stage fungal infections with similar visual spots.

Edge Deep Learning Memory: Executing multi-class image classification on microcontrollers with constrained RAM.

4. Technical Requirements & Deliverables

Hardware: ESP32-CAM / Raspberry Pi 4 with Camera Module, TFT Display Shield.

Vision Model: Fine-tuned MobileNetV3 / EfficientNet-Lite model trained on agricultural leaf disease datasets (e.g., PlantVillage).

On-Device Application: Lightweight UI rendering visual bounding boxes, infection severity ratings, and treatment cards.

5. Evaluation Metrics & Success Criteria

problem_statements.title: Smart Electrical Distribution Box Thermal & Overload Monitor
problem_statements.domain: Electrical Safety, Building Automation, & Fire Prevention
problem_statements.description:
Primary Goal: Prevent electrical panel fires by continuously monitoring breaker temperatures using non-contact infrared thermal sensors and current transducers.

1. Business Context & Problem Description

Electrical distribution boards in commercial and industrial buildings are major sources of structural fires due to loose wire connections, phase imbalances, and circuit overloads. Thermal imaging inspections are typically performed manually once a year. Continuous IoT thermal tracking catches loose connections and thermal runaway long before smoke develops.

2. Core Objectives

Measure surface temperature across electrical circuit breaker terminals using array-based thermal infrared sensors.

Measure current flow across phases using non-contact current sensors to flag phase imbalance.

Sound local buzzer alarms and trip main safety contactors if terminal temperatures exceed critical thresholds ().

Push thermal heatmaps and load metrics to a facility safety portal.

3. Key Technical Challenges

Low-Resolution Thermal Segmentation: Extracting accurate component temperatures from low-cost array sensors ( or  pixels).

Enclosure Installation: Mounting sensor arrays securely inside crowded breaker boxes without interfering with high-voltage wiring.

Noise Filtering: Distinguishing normal load heating from dangerous thermal runaway caused by high contact resistance.

4. Technical Requirements & Deliverables

Hardware: ESP32, AMG8833 () or MLX90640 () IR Thermal Array Sensor, SCT-013 Current Sensors, Relay Contactor Trigger, Piezo Buzzer.

Processing Engine: Bilinear interpolation of thermal arrays, dynamic hotspot tracking, and temperature gradient analysis.

Alert System: Visual thermal heatmap UI, local alarm output, and instant SMS/Email notification integration.

5. Evaluation Metrics & Success Criteria

problem_statements.title: IoT Smart Waste Bin Fill-Level & Route Optimization Engine
problem_statements.description:
Primary Goal: Optimize garbage truck collection routes by continuously monitoring public trash bin fill levels and tilt status using low-cost ultrasonic sensor nodes.

1. Business Context & Problem Description

Municipal waste collection trucks follow fixed daily routes, frequently visiting empty public trash bins while overflowing bins in high-traffic areas go unserviced. This leads to wasted fuel, higher vehicular emissions, and unhygienic street conditions. Real-time bin level tracking optimizes collection routes so trucks visit only bins requiring immediate emptying.

2. Core Objectives

Measure trash level height inside municipal bins using battery-powered ultrasonic sensors.

Detect bin tipping or vandalism events using internal tilt/accelerometer sensors.

Transmit bin status updates to a central platform once or twice daily over low-power cellular/LoRa links.

Generate dynamic, prioritized collection routes for waste vehicle drivers based on real-time bin priority queues.

3. Key Technical Challenges

Non-Uniform Trash Surfaces: Handling uneven garbage disposal profiles (e.g., crumpled paper, bottles) that scatter ultrasonic signals.

Ultra-Low Power Operations: Achieving multi-year battery life on field nodes exposed to harsh outdoor weather.

Rugged Enclosures: Protecting sensors from humidity, trash residue, foul odors, and physical vandalism.

4. Technical Requirements & Deliverables

Hardware: ESP32-CAM / ATmega328P / Low-Power MCU, HC-SR04 / JSN-SR04T Waterproof Ultrasonic Sensor, MPU6050 Accelerometer, SIM7000E NB-IoT/LTE-M module.

Firmware: Deep-sleep firmware waking nodes on timed intervals or tilt interrupts.

Route Engine: Cloud portal rendering fill-level maps and computing shortest-path vehicle routes (TSP algorithm).

5. Evaluation Metrics & Success Criteria

problem_statements.title: Computer Vision Smart Belt Conveyor Sorting System
problem_statements.description:
Primary Goal: Identify, classify, and sort packages moving on a conveyor belt based on shape, color, or barcode using a webcam and servo-driven diverter arms.

1. Business Context & Problem Description

High-throughput distribution hubs spend significant resources manually sorting packages, parcels, and manufactured parts into destination chutes. Industrial sorting systems are cost-prohibitive for small and medium enterprises. An affordable, camera-driven conveyor sorter automates item routing using low-cost microcontrollers and servomotors.

2. Core Objectives

Detect objects arriving on a moving conveyor belt using a camera feed.

Classify objects by dimensional footprint, color signature, or visual barcode/QR code data.

Calculate object travel speed and timing to actuate mechanical servo diverters at the exact arrival moment.

Track hourly sorting counts and error rates on a local control panel.

3. Key Technical Challenges

Motion Blur: Processing sharp object frames from moving conveyor belts under standard indoor lighting.

Precise Actuation Timing: Synchronizing visual detection events with mechanical servo arm triggers.

Variable Object Geometry: Classifying soft-packaged mailers, polybags, and irregular cardboard boxes accurately.

4. Technical Requirements & Deliverables

Hardware: Raspberry Pi 4 / PC workstation, High-frame-rate USB Webcam, PCA9685 Servo Driver board, TowerPro MG996R Servomotors / Solenoid actuators, Conveyor assembly.

Vision Pipeline: OpenCV contour extraction, color histogram matching, 1D/2D Barcode decoder module, and tracking algorithm.

Control Software: High-precision timer thread issuing servo actuation commands mapped to conveyor speed.

5. Evaluation Metrics & Success Criteria

problem_statements.title: IoT Smart Vibration & Health Monitor for Rotating Machinery
problem_statements.domain: Plant Maintenance, Heavy Industry, & Asset Performance
problem_statements.description:
Primary Goal: Track mechanical vibration spectra on pump shafts, fans, and gearboxes using MEMS accelerometers to detect bearing wear, shaft imbalance, and misalignment.

1. Business Context & Problem Description

Unplanned downtime caused by bearing failure or shaft misalignment in industrial machinery leads to costly production halts. Traditional manual vibration audits using handheld meters are performed intermittently, missing rapid wear escalation. Continuous vibration tracking using surface-mounted MEMS sensors catches mechanical wear in its earliest stages.

2. Core Objectives

Measure high-frequency tri-axial acceleration vibrations on motor casings and bearing housings.

Compute peak acceleration, velocity RMS, and Fast Fourier Transform (FFT) frequency spectra on edge hardware.

Compare measured RMS values against ISO 10816 industrial vibration severity standards.

Send automated alert flags when vibration levels enter "Unsatisfactory" or "Unacceptable" operating zones.

3. Key Technical Challenges

Sampling Bandwidth Limits: Sampling MEMS accelerometers at high frequencies () to capture subtle bearing pass frequencies.

Sensor Mounting Rigidity: Ensuring firm mechanical coupling (magnetic or stud mount) to eliminate vibration dampening.

Data Volume Reduction: Processing raw vibration streams on edge nodes to stream only spectral summaries and health indices.

4. Technical Requirements & Deliverables

Hardware: ESP32, ADXL345 / MPU6050 High-Speed Tri-Axial Accelerometer (I2C/SPI), Magnetic Mounting Base, OLED status display.

Edge Processing Engine: On-device Fast Fourier Transform (FFT) library extracting peak vibration frequencies and overall RMS velocity.

Maintenance Portal: Dashboard displaying real-time vibration wave plots, FFT spectral peaks, and ISO status gauges.

5. Evaluation Metrics & Success Criteria

problem_statements.title: Edge Computer Vision Smart Traffic Light Controller
problem_statements.domain: Intelligent Transportation Systems, Urban Planning, & Traffic Management
problem_statements.description:
Primary Goal: Dynamically adjust traffic light green-time durations at intersections based on real-time vehicle queue lengths measured by edge AI camera nodes.

1. Business Context & Problem Description

Static timer-based traffic lights cause unnecessary traffic congestion, fuel waste, and emergency vehicle delays because signal timings do not adjust to real-time traffic demand. Equipping intersections with camera-based edge vision nodes measures vehicle counts per lane dynamically, adjusting signal timing to clear congested lanes efficiently.

2. Core Objectives

Monitor vehicle queues across intersection lanes using overhead camera feeds.

Count vehicles per lane and classify vehicle types (cars, buses, motorcycles, trucks) using edge object detection.

Compute optimal green-light duration dynamically based on real-time lane congestion ratios.

Detect incoming emergency vehicles (ambulances, fire engines) to grant immediate green wave priority.

3. Key Technical Challenges

Occlusion in Dense Queues: Accurately counting bumper-to-bumper vehicles in packed lane queues.

Low-Latency Switching: Executing object detection and light control logic fast enough to adjust cycles smoothly.

Fail-Safe Operation: Defaulting instantly to standard fixed timer hardware logic if camera or compute hardware fails.

4. Technical Requirements & Deliverables

Hardware: Raspberry Pi 4 / NVIDIA Jetson Nano, RTSP IP Cameras / USB Webcams, 4-Channel Relay Board driving traffic signal lamps.

Vision Pipeline: Lightweight object detection model (YOLOv8-Nano / MobileNet-SSD) trained on vehicle datasets.

Signal Scheduling Engine: Dynamic green-time allocation algorithm balancing lane priority queues and maximum wait times.

5. Evaluation Metrics & Success Criteria

problem_statements.title: Smart Water Quality Sensing Station for Inland Aquafarms
problem_statements.description:
Primary Goal: Monitor pH, Dissolved Oxygen (DO), temperature, and water clarity in fish and shrimp ponds continuously to automate aerator pumps and prevent mass die-offs.

1. Business Context & Problem Description

Commercial fish and shrimp farming requires maintaining strict water quality limits. Sudden drops in Dissolved Oxygen (DO) levels or extreme pH fluctuations cause high aquatic mortality within hours. Manual chemical test kits are used irregularly, often failing to detect dangerous night-time oxygen drops. Continuous IoT sensing protects stock and automates aeration routines.

2. Core Objectives

Submerge sensor probes to measure water pH, Dissolved Oxygen (DO), temperature, and Total Dissolved Solids (TDS) continuously.

Actuate pond paddle-wheel aerator motors automatically via heavy-duty relays when oxygen levels drop.

Alert fish farmers via automated phone calls/SMS when parameters breach critical aquatic safety thresholds.

Stream historical water quality data to a central cloud dashboard for feeding and harvest optimization.

3. Key Technical Challenges

Probe Bio-Fouling: Preventing algae growth on sensitive pH and DO glass electrodes during extended submersion.

Signal Isolation: Eliminating electrical ground loops in water that distort analog sensor readings from multiple probes.

Sensor Calibration Routine: Simplifying multi-point calibration procedures for non-technical farm operators.

4. Technical Requirements & Deliverables

Hardware: ESP32, Analog pH Sensor kit, Analog Dissolved Oxygen Sensor kit, DS18B20 Waterproof Temp Sensor, Analog TDS Sensor, Heavy-Duty Relay Contactor.

Analog Conditioning: Signal isolation boards preventing inter-probe electrical interference.

Monitoring Portal: Web platform and SMS integration displaying live water health metrics, aeration logs, and calibration wizards.

5. Evaluation Metrics & Success Criteria

problem_statements.title: AI Speech-Guided Edge Voice Assistant for Machine Operation
problem_statements.description:
Primary Goal: Control industrial machines, lathes, and assembly equipment using local, offline voice commands processed completely on an edge microcontroller without cloud latency or privacy risks.

1. Business Context & Problem Description

Operators running industrial machinery often have both hands occupied with parts or safety tools, making manual button/touchscreen interaction slow and awkward. Cloud-based voice assistants (e.g., Alexa, Google Assistant) are unacceptable in industrial environments due to network latency, cloud dependency, and privacy risks. A fully offline edge voice controller enables secure, hands-free operation.

2. Core Objectives

Capture operator voice commands using a noise-canceling directional microphone array.

Process speech recognition completely offline on an edge microcontroller/processor node.

Recognize specific operational wake words and command phrases (e.g., "Start Conveyor", "Emergency Pause", "Set Speed 5").

Trigger digital output pins and motor relays to actuate machinery directly with sub-second response times.

3. Key Technical Challenges

Heavy Factory Ambient Noise: Filtering out background motor hum, mechanical clatter, and adjacent voices ( environments).

Zero Cloud Latency: Executing Speech-to-Text (STT) and intent matching locally within tight microchip memory constraints.

Safety & False Command Prevention: Preventing unintended machine actuation caused by misheard background speech.

4. Technical Requirements & Deliverables

Hardware: ESP32-S3 / Raspberry Pi 4, I2S MEMS Microphone Array module (e.g., INMP441 / ReSpeaker 2-Mics Shield), 4-Channel Relay Output module.

Offline Speech Engine: Lightweight keyword spotting (KWS) and intent parsing engine (e.g., MicroSpeech / PocketSphinx / Picovoice Porcupine local runtime).

Machine Control Interface: Direct GPIO hardware output map triggering relays and motor drivers accompanied by audio confirmation beeps.

5. Evaluation Metrics & Success Criteria

problem_statements.title: Non-Invasive Water Pipeline Corrosion & Flow Analytics
problem_statements.description:
Primary Goal: Estimate internal pipe degradation, scale buildup, and flow velocity non-invasively using surface-mounted acoustic/vibration sensors and edge signal processing.

1. Business Context & Problem Description

Municipal and industrial water networks suffer from unseen internal pipe corrosion and mineral scaling, leading to catastrophic bursts or restricted flow rates. Excavating or cutting open pressurized pipes to inspect their interior is prohibitively expensive and disruptive. Strapping low-cost piezo acoustic sensors onto external pipe walls allows data scientists to infer internal structural degradation and fluid flow dynamics from structural resonance changes.

2. Core Objectives

Capture acoustic resonance and flow-induced vibration signals from external pipe walls non-invasively.

Isolate structural resonance frequencies to detect wall thinning, internal pitting, and heavy mineral scale accumulation.

Estimate fluid flow rates continuously from flow-generated turbulences.

Stream pipe health indices and maintenance alerts to a centralized utility management dashboard.

3. Key Technical Challenges

Acoustic Attenuation: Disambiguating fluid turbulence noise from structural resonance shifts caused by wall thinning.

Pipe Material Variability: Calibrating baseline acoustic propagation velocities across PVC, galvanized iron, and copper pipes.

Low-Power Continuous Sensing: Executing Fast Fourier Transforms (FFT) on low-power microcontrollers without draining field battery packs.

4. Technical Requirements & Deliverables

Hardware: ESP32, Piezoelectric Contact Vibration Sensors (e.g., LDT0-028K), MAX9814 Preamplifier Modules, Strap-on Pipe Clamps.

Signal Pipeline: Bandpass filtering, Fast Fourier Transform (FFT) spectrum extraction, and resonance shift detection logic.

Utility Portal: Dashboard displaying pipe wall health scores, estimated flow rates, and maintenance dispatch triggers.

5. Evaluation Metrics & Success Criteria

problem_statements.title: Edge Computer Vision Livestock Health & Rumination Tracker
problem_statements.description:
Primary Goal: Track livestock rumination cycles, jaw movement, and early lethargy signs in dairy cattle using an overhead low-cost webcam and edge computer vision.

1. Business Context & Problem Description

Rumination (cud-chewing) duration is the single most critical early indicator of metabolic health, stress, and impending illness in dairy cows. Traditional monitoring relies on expensive wearable smart collars or manual observation by farm hands. An overhead edge vision camera installed above feeding stalls automatically tracks head/jaw motions across multiple cattle simultaneously, democratizing precision livestock monitoring.

2. Core Objectives

Track cattle head locations and jaw movement frequencies in feeding stalls using overhead camera feeds.

Classify real-time activities into eating, ruminating, resting, or abnormal lethargic behavior.

Calculate daily cumulative rumination time per tagged cow stall.

Send automated mobile alerts to farmers when a cow's rumination time drops by  below its baseline.

3. Key Technical Challenges

Subtle Jaw Motion Detection: Detecting fine repetitive jaw movements from a distance under varying stable illumination.

Animal Movement & Occlusion: Maintaining cow tracking when animals shift positions or overlap in stall views.

Edge Resource Limits: Running multi-object head tracking and temporal motion analysis on low-cost hardware.

4. Technical Requirements & Deliverables

Hardware: Raspberry Pi 4 / PC Workstation, Generic RTSP IP Camera / USB Webcam.

Vision Model: Optical flow estimation or lightweight pose/keypoint detector (e.g., MediaPipe/YOLO-Pose) tracking head/mouth movement frequencies.

Alert Portal: Mobile-friendly dashboard rendering cow health logs, daily rumination charts, and anomaly flags.

5. Evaluation Metrics & Success Criteria

problem_statements.title: Smart Acoustic Transformer Arcing & Corona Discharge Monitor
problem_statements.domain: Power Utilities, Electrical Grid Safety, & Predictive Maintenance
problem_statements.description:
Primary Goal: Detect silent electrical arcing and corona discharge in high-voltage substations and electrical cabinets using ultrasonic acoustic sensors and edge pattern recognition.

1. Business Context & Problem Description

High-voltage electrical transformers, switchgears, and distribution panels experience insulation breakdown that manifests as high-frequency electrical arcing or corona discharge before catastrophic explosion or blackout events occur. Because corona discharge emits sound primarily in the ultrasonic spectrum (), it is completely silent to human ears. Low-cost ultrasonic microphones capture these hidden emissions early.

2. Core Objectives

Continuous monitoring of electrical enclosures using high-frequency ultrasonic acoustic transducers.

Down-mix and analyze ultrasonic emissions () on edge hardware using heterodyne or digital signal processing algorithms.

Distinguish dangerous electrical arcing/corona signatures from benign mechanical noise (cooling fans, wind).

Trigger immediate circuit breaker isolation relays and alert utility operators upon arcing detection.

3. Key Technical Challenges

High-Frequency Sampling Requirements: Interfacing ultrasonic transducers requiring high-speed analog sampling without high-cost Oscilloscopes or DAQs.

Acoustic Noise Rejection: Eliminating ambient high-frequency acoustic noise generated by nearby machinery or pressure leaks.

Arcing vs. Corona Differentiation: Classifying the severity of insulation breakdowns based on acoustic pulse patterns.

4. Technical Requirements & Deliverables

Hardware: ESP32-S3 / Raspberry Pi Pico, Ultrasonic MEMS Microphone / Transducer (e.g., Knowles SPU0410LR5H), 12V Relay Contactor.

DSP Framework: On-device Fast Fourier Transform (FFT) spectral power density analyzer targeting  bands.

Grid Safety Portal: Central web platform logging discharge intensity decibels, timestamped event logs, and breaker status.

5. Evaluation Metrics & Success Criteria

problem_statements.title: Optical Computer Vision Smart Counterfeit Currency & Document Inspector
problem_statements.description:
Primary Goal: Verify paper currency authenticity, security thread patterns, and document UV watermark signatures using an off-the-shelf camera module and multi-spectral LED lighting.

1. Business Context & Problem Description

Counterfeit currency notes and forged identity documents cause significant financial losses for small retailers, transport hubs, and banking kiosks. Professional UV counterfeit detectors are costly and require trained human operators to manually verify watermarks under specialized light. An automated, low-cost multi-spectral camera module automatically validates notes and credentials within seconds.

2. Core Objectives

Illuminate banknotes or documents sequentially under White, Ultraviolet (UV-A), and Infrared (IR) LEDs using micro-controllers.

Capture multi-spectral image frames using a standard camera module without IR-cut filters.

Analyze fluorescent security threads, micro-printing, and optical variable ink patterns using computer vision.

Display instant "PASS / FAIL / COUNTERFEIT" flags on an onboard display screen.

3. Key Technical Challenges

Multi-Spectral LED Synchronization: Precisely synchronizing multi-color LED switching with camera frame exposure triggers.

Image Alignment & Registration: Compensating for slight manual placement offsets of banknotes under the camera.

Wear and Tear Degradation: Distinguishing truly counterfeit notes from genuine, worn, dirty, or folded currency notes.

4. Technical Requirements & Deliverables

Hardware: ESP32-CAM / Raspberry Pi Zero 2W (NoIR Camera), UV-A () LEDs, IR () LEDs, White LEDs,  OLED Display.

Vision Pipeline: Multi-frame feature extraction checking UV fluorescence intensity, watermark contours, and dimensional aspects.

Retail UI Engine: Standalone device firmware running complete local inference with zero internet requirement.

5. Evaluation Metrics & Success Criteria

problem_statements.title: IoT Smart Grain Storage Silo Temperature & Humidity Probe Vector
problem_statements.domain: Agriculture Storage, Food Security, & Supply Chain
problem_statements.description:
Primary Goal: Prevent grain spoilage and fungal rot inside agricultural storage silos using a cable-suspended array of digital temperature and humidity sensors.

1. Business Context & Problem Description

Post-harvest grain loss in storage silos due to moisture accumulation, fungal rot, and insect infestation affects millions of tons of food annually. Moisture pockets create localized "hotspots" where grain fermenting produces destructive heat. Suspending a low-cost multiplexed cable array of digital temperature/humidity sensors down silo centers enables early detection of internal spoilage pockets.

2. Core Objectives

Measure multi-depth temperature and relative humidity continuously along vertical grain column profiles.

Compute equilibrium grain moisture content (EMC) using psychrometric equations on edge microcontrollers.

Identify localized thermal hotspots indicating early fungal fermentation or pest activity.

Actuate aeration fans automatically to equalize silo moisture and dissipate internal heat build-up.

3. Key Technical Challenges

Dust & Mechanical Wear: Protecting low-cost sensor nodes from high abrasion, grain dust, and mechanical pressure during loading.

One-Wire Bus Scalability: Reading dozens of digital sensors connected across long vertical cables () without data corruption.

Early Hotspot Localization: Detecting localized thermal spikes before heat diffuses across large surrounding grain volumes.

4. Technical Requirements & Deliverables

Hardware: ESP32, Waterproof DS18B20 Temperature Sensors / SHT30 Sensors multiplexed along suspended cables, 12V Relay driving aeration fans.

Firmware: One-Wire bus protocol reader, 3D temperature matrix interpolation, and automatic fan control routines.

Silo Dashboard: Web interface rendering vertical temperature/humidity heatmaps per silo with automated alert logs.

5. Evaluation Metrics & Success Criteria

problem_statements.title: Smart Optical Sensor Fluid Contamination & Turbidity Analyzer
problem_statements.description:
Primary Goal: Detect particulate degradation, water contamination, and clarity loss in industrial lubricants, hydraulic oils, and coolant fluids using a low-cost optical sensor module.

1. Business Context & Problem Description

Hydraulic fluid, engine oil, and industrial coolants break down over time due to metallic wear debris, soot, chemical oxidation, and water ingress. Running machinery with degraded fluids leads to severe mechanical wear and catastrophic pump/engine failures. An inline optical sensor measuring multi-wavelength light transmission provides real-time fluid health tracking.

2. Core Objectives

Measure light attenuation and scattering across fluid channels using multi-wavelength LEDs (Red, Green, Blue, IR) and photodiode receivers.

Calculate fluid turbidity, soot concentration, and water emulsion indices in real time.

Track rate-of-degradation trends to predict fluid replacement dates dynamically.

Trigger maintenance warnings when fluid opacity or contamination crosses critical safety limits.

3. Key Technical Challenges

Fluid Viscosity & Bubbles: Filtering out false optical drops caused by transient entrained air bubbles in moving fluid lines.

Optical Window Staining: Compensating for gradual residue buildup on optical glass sensor windows over time.

Multi-Fluid Calibration: Adjusting baseline optical absorption profiles across different oil grades and synthetic coolants.

4. Technical Requirements & Deliverables

Hardware: ESP32 / Arduino Nano, TSL2591 High-Dynamic-Range Light Sensor / TSL230R, Multi-wavelength LED cluster, Transparent inline flow cell.

DSP Framework: Ratio-metric optical absorption modeling, baseline drift compensation algorithms, and moving-average filters.

Maintenance UI: Digital health score display (), estimated remaining fluid life indicator, and alert log output.

5. Evaluation Metrics & Success Criteria

problem_statements.title: Edge AI Computer Vision Smart Wildlife Crossing & Intrusion Warning
problem_statements.description:
Primary Goal: Detect wild animals approaching road corridors or farm perimeters at night using thermal/infrared camera feeds and trigger localized deterrents or motorist warnings.

1. Business Context & Problem Description

Wildlife-vehicle collisions along rural highways cause human casualties, severe vehicle damage, and animal deaths. Furthermore, wild animals intruding into agricultural fields destroy valuable crops overnight. Traditional fencing is expensive and restricts natural migratory paths. An edge vision warning system detects animal approaches and triggers warning lights for drivers or humane acoustic deterrents for crops.

2. Core Objectives

Capture roadside/perimeter imagery using low-cost Infrared (IR) night-vision or low-resolution thermal cameras.

Detect and classify wild animals (e.g., deer, wild boars, elephants, cattle) approaching road edges or farm perimeters.

Activate roadside LED flashing hazard signs to warn approaching motorists in real time.

Trigger directional ultrasonic frequency bursts to humanely deter crop-raiding animals from entering fields.

3. Key Technical Challenges

Low-Resolution Night Imagery: Detecting moving animal shapes in grainy IR or low-resolution thermal frames ( or ).

False Triggers: Rejecting non-target movements such as wind-blown tree branches or small rodents.

Solar Battery Operations: Operating continuous night surveillance on small solar-recharged power packs.

4. Technical Requirements & Deliverables

Hardware: ESP32-CAM (IR-cut removed) + IR Illuminator / Raspberry Pi + MLX90640 Thermal Sensor, High-Power Flashing LED Relays, Piezo Ultrasonic Speaker.

Vision Model: Quantized lightweight object classifier or motion-blob shape analysis model running locally on edge hardware.

Forestry Dashboard: Wireless event logger transmitting GPS location, timestamped intrusion snapshots, and animal classification counts.

5. Evaluation Metrics & Success Criteria

problem_statements.title: Smart Electrical Sub-Station Thermal Arc Flash & Temperature Mapper
problem_statements.domain: Industrial Safety, Power Distribution, & Facility Management
problem_statements.description:
Primary Goal: Map surface thermal distribution across high-power busbars and connection lugs continuously using non-contact infrared array sensors to prevent arc flashes.

1. Business Context & Problem Description

Electrical arc flashes in high-power distribution panels occur when loose mechanical busbar joints or degraded contacts overheat, ionizing surrounding air and creating explosive short circuits. Manual thermography inspections performed once a year miss rapidly deteriorating connection joints. Continuous thermal array monitoring provides non-contact, real-time heat mapping inside electrical enclosures.

2. Core Objectives

Continuous thermal imaging of internal distribution busbars and terminal connections using non-contact IR matrix sensors.

Interpolate low-resolution thermal data to render continuous  temperature heatmaps of the breaker panel interior.

Track individual terminal connection temperatures against dynamic ambient baseline values.

Trigger emergency circuit breaker isolation relays before connections reach critical flashover temperatures ().

3. Key Technical Challenges

Emissivity Variances: Adjusting surface temperature calculations across shiny copper busbars, dull steel bolts, and plastic wire insulation.

Enclosure Space Limits: Wide-angle thermal mapping inside tightly cramped distribution boxes without blind spots.

Thermal Transient Rejection: Distinguishing normal, temporary current load heat spikes from dangerous contact resistance heating.

4. Technical Requirements & Deliverables

Hardware: ESP32-S3, MLX90640 () / AMG8833 Thermal Array Sensor, 12V Contactor Relay, Local Piezo Alarm.

Software Engine: Dynamic thermal frame interpolation (Bicubic/RBF), temperature anomaly boundary extraction, and historical drift analysis.

Safety Dashboard: Local screen and web interface rendering color-coded thermal maps with localized connection temperature tags.

5. Evaluation Metrics & Success Criteria

problem_statements.title: Computer Vision Automated Micro-Solder Joint Defect Inspector
problem_statements.domain: Electronics Manufacturing, PCB Assembly, & Quality Control
problem_statements.description:
Primary Goal: Inspect micro-solder joints on surface-mount technology (SMT) printed circuit boards using a USB microscope camera and edge computer vision.

1. Business Context & Problem Description

Defective solder joints (e.g., solder bridges, tombstoning, cold joints, insufficient solder) on SMT Printed Circuit Boards (PCBs) cause costly product failures during field operation. Commercial Automated Optical Inspection (AOI) machines cost tens of thousands of dollars, placing them out of reach for small electronics manufacturers and prototyping labs. A desktop camera inspector provides fast, automated solder defect verification at a fraction of the cost.

2. Core Objectives

Capture high-magnification images of PCB solder pads using a low-cost USB digital microscope camera.

Segment individual component pads and solder joints using computer vision techniques.

Classify solder joint quality into specific defect categories (e.g., Good, Solder Bridge, Cold Joint, Missing Component, Tombstone).

Highlight defect locations visually on a digital PCB placement overlay for operator rework.

3. Key Technical Challenges

Specular Reflection Glare: Managing extreme light reflections off metallic, curved solder surfaces under bright LED lighting.

Micro-Scale Precision: Detecting minute solder bridges measuring down to fractions of a millimeter ().

Varied Component Geometry: Adapting to diverse component packages (0603, 0805, QFN, SOIC) without requiring re-training.

4. Technical Requirements & Deliverables

Hardware: Raspberry Pi 4 / PC Workstation, Generic  USB Digital Microscope Camera, Ring LED Light Attachment.

Vision Model: Fine-tuned lightweight object detection / classification network (e.g., YOLO-Nano / MobileNetV3) trained on PCB defect datasets.

Rework UI: Desktop GUI displaying zoom overlays, color-coded bounding boxes around defective joints, and automated inspection logs.

5. Evaluation Metrics & Success Criteria

problem_statements.title: IoT Smart Soil Salinity & Nutrient Leaching Monitor
problem_statements.domain: Precision Agriculture, Soil Health, & Land Management
problem_statements.description:
Primary Goal: Track soil electrical conductivity (EC), salt accumulation, and fertilizer leaching in greenhouse crops using low-cost multi-depth electrodes.

1. Business Context & Problem Description

Over-fertilization leads to soil salinization, root burn, and chemical leaching into local groundwater, ruining agricultural land and wasting expensive fertilizers. Traditional soil testing requires sending physical samples to laboratories, taking days or weeks for results. Continuous soil Electrical Conductivity (EC) sensing at multi-depth root zones allows farmers to optimize fertilizer application in real time.

2. Core Objectives

Measure soil Electrical Conductivity (EC), Volumetric Water Content (VWC), and soil temperature at root level continuously.
